title: Saffron and Chilli Rouille with Toasts
summary: Garlic pounded with saffron, cayenne and tomato purée, emulsified with yolks and oil, served on baked baguette toasts.

ingredients.item: garlic cloves, halved, green shoots removed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Pound the garlic with the salt to a smooth paste, then pound in the saffron, cayenne and tomato purée.

steps.title: Add the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks into the paste in a bowl set on a damp towel.

steps.title: Add the oil
steps.text: Add the sunflower oil drop by drop, whisking all the time, then in a thin stream once it thickens. Finish with the olive oil a spoonful at a time.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Bake the baguette slices at 200 °C for 8-10 min until golden, then top with rouille or float on fish soup.

tips: Crumble the saffron finely so the colour spreads evenly.
Add more cayenne for a hotter sauce.
safety: Use pasteurised eggs; pregnant women, young children, older people and anyone unwell should skip raw-egg sauces.
For a cooked-yolk version, heat the yolks with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp water over simmering water to 71 °C first.
storage: Keep the rouille covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; toasts in a tin for 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
